_about: Safe home-care steps for common minor problems, written in simple language for Indian families. Each item lists self-care steps, things to avoid, red flags (when to get urgent help) and when to see a doctor. Steps are taken from public guidance (WHO, NHS, CDC, AAP, ICMR, MoHFW). The file has no medicine names, no doses and no herbal dosing. Use it for education only.
disclaimer: This is general self-care information, not a diagnosis or treatment. If you are unsure, if you are pregnant, if the person is a baby, a child or an older adult, or if they have a long-term illness, talk to a doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medicine without your doctor. In an emergency, call 112, or 108 for an ambulance.

items.title: Common cold
items.summary: A cold is a viral infection of the nose and throat that usually gets better on its own in 7 to 10 days.
self_care: Rest and sleep well.
Drink plenty of fluids such as water, warm soups and warm water with lemon.
Breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, but keep children away from hot water to prevent burns.
For adults and children over 1 year, a spoon of honey in warm water may soothe the throat.
Wash your hands often and cover coughs and sneezes to protect others.
avoid: Do not give honey to babies under 1 year old.
Do not take antibiotics for a cold unless a doctor prescribes them. Antibiotics do not work on cold viruses.
Avoid smoking and smoky rooms.
red_flags: Trouble breathing, fast breathing or chest pain: call 112 or 108 now.
Lips or face turning blue or grey: call 112 now.
A baby under 3 months with a fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or more.
Very high fever, confusion, or being very hard to wake.
Fever with a stiff neck or a rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass.
see_doctor_if: Symptoms last more than 10 days or keep getting worse.
You have diabetes, heart, lung or kidney disease, or a weak immune system.
Ear pain, pain over the cheeks or forehead, or thick green mucus with fever.
sources: AAP (HealthyChildren.org): honey not for infants under 12 months

items.title: Sore throat
items.summary: Most sore throats are caused by viruses and get better within about a week.
self_care: Gargle with warm salt water (about half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water). Adults and older children only.
Drink warm fluids and plenty of water.
Eat soft, cool or warm foods that are easy to swallow.
For adults and children over 1 year, a spoon of honey may soothe the throat.
Rest your voice and avoid smoke.
avoid: Do not give honey to babies under 1 year old.
Do not ask young children to gargle, because they may swallow the water or choke.
Do not take leftover or shared antibiotics.
red_flags: Difficulty breathing or noisy breathing: call 112 or 108 now.
Cannot swallow saliva or is drooling.
Cannot open the mouth fully, or there is swelling on one side of the throat or neck.
Very high fever, or feeling very unwell.
Signs of dehydration: very little urine, very dry mouth, dizziness.
see_doctor_if: The sore throat lasts more than 1 week or keeps coming back.
Fever with white patches on the tonsils and no cough.
You have a weak immune system, for example from cancer treatment.
sources: NICE NG84: Sore throat (acute) antimicrobial prescribing

items.title: Dry cough
items.summary: A dry cough often follows a cold and usually gets better within 3 weeks.
self_care: Drink plenty of warm fluids and water.
For adults and children over 1 year, a spoon of honey in warm water may ease the cough.
Breathe in steam, or keep the room air less dry. Keep children away from hot water.
Rest, and raise your head with an extra pillow at night.
Stay away from smoke, dust and strong smells.
avoid: Do not give honey to babies under 1 year old.
Do not smoke, and keep children away from smoke.
Do not give any cough medicine to young children without a doctor's advice.
red_flags: Severe breathlessness, chest pain or blue lips: call 112 or 108 now.
Coughing up blood.
A child who makes a 'whoop' sound or turns blue during coughing fits.
High fever with fast breathing.
Sudden cough after choking on food or a small object.
see_doctor_if: The cough lasts more than 3 weeks.
Weight loss, night sweats or fever with a long cough. These can be signs of TB, which needs a test.
You have asthma, COPD, heart disease or diabetes and the cough is getting worse.

items.title: Acidity / heartburn
items.summary: Heartburn is a burning feeling in the chest when stomach acid comes back up. It is often linked to food and habits.
self_care: Eat smaller meals more often instead of large meals.
Finish your dinner at least 3 hours before lying down.
Raise the head end of your bed by 10 to 20 cm.
Notice which foods trigger it (for example very spicy, oily or fried food, coffee, alcohol) and cut down on them.
If you are overweight, losing weight slowly may help.
Stop smoking. Ask your doctor for help to quit.
avoid: Do not lie down or bend over right after eating.
Avoid tight belts and clothes around the waist.
Do not assume chest pain is acidity. Heart pain can feel like a burning in the chest.
red_flags: Chest pain or pressure that spreads to the arm, jaw, neck or back, or comes with sweating or breathlessness: call 112 or 108 now. This may be a heart attack.
Vomiting blood, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
Black, tarry stools.
Food getting stuck when you swallow, or pain when swallowing.
Weight loss without trying.
see_doctor_if: You have heartburn most days for more than 3 weeks.
You are over 55 and the symptoms are new.
Home steps do not help.
sources: NICE CG184: Dyspepsia and GORD in adults
American Heart Association: Warning signs of a heart attack

items.title: Constipation
items.summary: Constipation means passing hard stools less often than usual. Diet, water and activity often help.
self_care: Slowly add more fibre: whole grains, millets, dal, vegetables, fruits like guava and papaya.
Drink enough water through the day.
Be active every day, for example a 20 to 30 minute walk.
Go to the toilet when you feel the urge. Do not hold it in.
Try a regular toilet time, such as after breakfast. Raising your feet on a small stool may help.
avoid: Do not use laxatives or enemas regularly without a doctor's advice.
Do not strain hard for a long time on the toilet.
Avoid eating mostly refined foods like maida, white bread and fried snacks.
red_flags: Severe belly pain with a swollen, hard belly and vomiting.
Cannot pass stool or gas at all, with belly swelling.
Blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools.
Constipation with fever and belly pain.
see_doctor_if: Constipation lasts more than 3 weeks, or your bowel habit changes for no clear reason.
Weight loss without trying, or feeling very tired.
It started after a new medicine. Talk to your doctor, and do not stop the medicine on your own.

items.title: Loose motions (diarrhoea)
items.summary: Loose motions are often caused by an infection and usually stop within a few days. The main danger is losing too much water.
self_care: Drink ORS (oral rehydration solution) made exactly as written on the WHO-ORS packet, in small sips after each loose motion.
Keep drinking other safe fluids too: boiled and cooled water, rice kanji, buttermilk, coconut water, dal water.
Keep eating light, normal food such as rice, curd rice, idli, khichdi or banana. Keep breastfeeding babies.
Wash hands with soap after using the toilet and before cooking or eating.
Watch how much urine is passed. Pale urine passed often is a good sign.
avoid: Do not use soft drinks, packaged fruit juice or glucose powder in place of ORS. Too much sugar can make loose motions worse.
Do not give medicines to stop loose motions to children unless a doctor advises it.
Do not stop feeding a child who has loose motions.
red_flags: Signs of dehydration: very little or no urine, very dry mouth, sunken eyes, dizziness, a child who is very sleepy or floppy.
Blood in the stool.
Cannot keep any fluids down because of vomiting.
High fever, or severe belly pain.
Watery motions like rice water in large amounts. This may be cholera, so go to a hospital now or call 108.
see_doctor_if: Loose motions last more than 2 days in adults or more than 1 day in a young child.
The person is elderly, pregnant, or has diabetes or kidney disease.
Loose motions keep coming back.
sources: MoHFW India: Stop Diarrhoea Campaign (ORS and zinc)

items.title: Mild fever
items.summary: Fever is the body fighting an infection. A mild fever with no warning signs can often be managed at home.
self_care: Rest, and drink plenty of fluids like water, ORS, soups and buttermilk.
Wear light clothes and keep the room cool and airy.
Wipe the forehead and body with a cloth soaked in normal-temperature (not cold) water if it helps comfort.
Check the temperature with a thermometer and write it down with the time.
If you need a medicine for fever, ask a doctor or pharmacist which one and how much is safe for you or your child.
avoid: Do not use ice-cold water or alcohol to sponge the body.
Do not wrap the person in heavy blankets.
Do not take antibiotics without a doctor's prescription.
red_flags: A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or more: see a doctor now.
Stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, a fit (seizure) or being very hard to wake: call 112 or 108 now.
Trouble breathing.
A rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass, or bleeding from the gums or nose.
Signs of dehydration: very little urine, very dry mouth, sunken eyes.
Fever of 40°C (104°F) or more.
see_doctor_if: Fever lasts more than 3 days. In India, a test for dengue, malaria or typhoid may be needed.
Fever keeps coming back, or comes with chills and shivering.
The person is elderly, pregnant, or has diabetes, kidney, heart or lung disease.
sources: WHO: Dengue and severe dengue fact sheet

items.title: Headache (tension type)
items.summary: A tension headache feels like a tight band around the head and is often linked to stress, poor sleep, hunger or screen time.
self_care: Drink a glass of water and eat if you have missed a meal.
Rest in a quiet, dim room.
Gently massage your neck, shoulders and temples, or put a warm cloth on your neck.
Take regular breaks from screens and check your sitting posture.
Try to sleep at the same time every night and manage stress, for example with slow breathing.
avoid: Do not take pain medicines on more than a few days a week without a doctor's advice. This can cause more headaches.
Avoid skipping meals and going without water for long.
red_flags: A sudden, very severe headache, like the worst ever: call 112 or 108 now.
Headache with weakness, numbness, drooping face, slurred speech or trouble seeing: call 112 now. This may be a stroke.
Headache with fever and stiff neck, or a rash.
Headache after a head injury, with vomiting or drowsiness.
Headache with confusion or a fit (seizure).
see_doctor_if: Headaches happen often or keep getting worse.
Headaches wake you up at night or are worst in the morning with vomiting.
You are over 50 and this is a new kind of headache, or you have high blood pressure.

items.title: Minor cuts and scrapes
items.summary: Small cuts and scrapes usually heal well if they are cleaned and kept covered.
self_care: Wash your hands first.
Press on the cut with a clean cloth for a few minutes to stop bleeding.
Rinse the wound under clean running water to remove dirt.
Cover it with a clean dressing or plaster, and change it daily or when it gets wet or dirty.
Watch for signs of infection over the next few days.
avoid: Do not put turmeric paste, coffee powder, mud, ash or toothpaste on a wound.
Do not blow on the wound or touch it with dirty hands.
Do not pull out an object stuck deep in the wound. Leave it and get medical help.
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure: call 108.
Blood spurting out of the wound: press hard and call 112 or 108 now.
A deep or gaping cut, or a cut on the face, eye or genitals.
Numbness or cannot move the finger or limb past the cut.
Animal or human bite. A dog, cat or monkey bite needs urgent rabies care the same day.
see_doctor_if: Signs of infection: growing redness, swelling, pus, warmth or fever.
The wound was dirty or from rusty metal and you are not sure your tetanus vaccine is up to date.
You have diabetes and the wound is on your foot, or it heals slowly.
sources: St John Ambulance / Indian Red Cross Society first aid guidance

items.title: Minor burns
items.summary: A small, shallow burn can be cared for at home if it is cooled quickly and kept clean.
self_care: Cool the burn under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible.
Remove rings, bangles, watches or tight clothing near the burn, unless they are stuck to the skin.
After cooling, cover the burn loosely with cling film or a clean, non-fluffy cloth.
Keep the person warm while you cool only the burned area.
Leave blisters alone and let them heal.
avoid: Do not put toothpaste, butter, oil, ghee, ice, turmeric or ink on a burn.
Do not use ice or ice-cold water.
Do not burst blisters or peel off loose skin.
Do not pull off clothing that is stuck to the burn.
red_flags: A burn larger than the person's palm: call 108 or go to hospital.
A burn on the face, hands, feet, genitals or over a joint.
A deep burn that looks white, brown or charred, or that does not hurt.
An electrical or chemical burn, or burns from a fire in a closed room (smoke breathed in): call 112 now.
Any burn in a baby, a young child, an older adult or a pregnant woman.
Trouble breathing, a hoarse voice, or burns in the mouth or nose: call 112 now.
see_doctor_if: The burn shows signs of infection: more pain, redness, swelling, pus or fever.
The burn has not healed in 2 weeks.
You are not sure your tetanus vaccine is up to date.
sources: British Burn Association first aid guidance (cool running water for 20 minutes)

items.title: Mouth ulcers
items.summary: Small, painful mouth ulcers are common and usually heal on their own within 1 to 2 weeks.
self_care: Rinse your mouth with warm salt water.
Use a soft toothbrush and brush gently.
Eat soft, cool foods such as curd, curd rice or idli.
Drink plenty of water, using a straw if it hurts.
Try to notice triggers such as stress, a sharp tooth, or biting the cheek.
avoid: Avoid very spicy, salty, sour or hot foods until it heals.
Do not chew tobacco, gutka or paan, and do not smoke.
Do not touch or scrape the ulcer.
red_flags: An ulcer or patch in the mouth that has not healed in 3 weeks. This needs a doctor or dentist check, especially if you use tobacco.
A red or white patch, or a lump in the mouth.
Cannot eat or drink, with signs of dehydration.
Mouth ulcers with a high fever, skin rash or blisters on the body or eyes.
see_doctor_if: Ulcers keep coming back often.
Ulcers are large, many, or very painful.
Ulcers come with tiredness, weight loss or loose motions.
sources: ICMR: National cancer registry programme reports on oral cancer

items.title: Muscle or joint sprain
items.summary: A sprain or strain is a stretch or small tear of a ligament or muscle. Most get better with rest and care over a few weeks.
self_care: Rest the injured part for the first 2 to 3 days. Avoid putting weight on it.
Put a cold pack or ice wrapped in a cloth on it for up to 20 minutes, every 2 to 3 hours. Never put ice straight on the skin.
Wrap it with a crepe bandage that is firm but not tight.
Keep the injured part raised above heart level when you can, for example on pillows.
After 2 to 3 days, start moving it gently as pain allows.
avoid: For the first 2 to 3 days, avoid heat such as hot water or hot packs, and avoid rubbing or massaging hard.
Do not get massage or bone-setting from untrained people.
Do not wrap the bandage so tight that fingers or toes turn blue, cold or numb.
red_flags: The limb looks bent or out of shape, or you heard a crack: get it checked today. It may be broken.
Cannot put any weight on the leg, or cannot move the joint at all.
Numbness, tingling, or cold, pale or blue fingers or toes.
Severe pain or swelling that keeps getting worse.
A swollen, painful calf with no clear injury, especially after a long journey or bed rest. Get urgent care.
see_doctor_if: It is not getting better after 1 week.
The joint feels loose or keeps giving way.
You have diabetes, or take blood-thinning medicines, and the swelling or bruising is large.
sources: St John Ambulance first aid guidance (RICE)

items.title: Mild dehydration / heat exhaustion
items.title_hi: पानी की कमी / गर्मी से थकान
items.summary: In hot weather the body can lose too much water and salt, causing tiredness, headache, dizziness and dark urine.
self_care: Move to a cool, shaded place and lie down with legs slightly raised.
Sip water, ORS, buttermilk, lemon water with a pinch of salt, or coconut water.
Loosen tight clothes and cool the skin with a wet cloth and a fan.
Rest for the day and avoid going out in the hottest hours (about 12 noon to 3 pm).
Drink water often in hot weather, even if you are not thirsty. Older adults may not feel thirst well.
avoid: Avoid alcohol, and drinks with a lot of sugar or caffeine, during a heatwave.
Do not leave children or older adults in a parked car or closed room.
Do not do heavy work or exercise in the midday sun.
red_flags: Confusion, fainting, a fit (seizure) or very hot skin: call 108 or 112 now. This may be heat stroke. Cool the person with water and a fan while you wait.
Body temperature of 40°C (104°F) or more.
No urine for 8 hours or more, or very dark urine.
Fast heartbeat, fast breathing, or cannot keep fluids down.
Not better after 30 minutes of rest and fluids in a cool place.
see_doctor_if: You get dizzy or tired often in the heat.
You have heart or kidney disease, or take water tablets (diuretics). Ask your doctor how much to drink in hot weather.
Muscle cramps last more than 1 hour.
sources: NDMA India: Heat wave do's and don'ts
WHO: Heat and health fact sheet

items.title: Poor sleep
items.summary: Trouble sleeping now and then is common. Simple daily habits can often improve sleep.
self_care: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, including weekends.
Keep your bedroom dark, quiet and cool.
Stop using phones and TV about 1 hour before bed.
Get daylight and some exercise during the day, but not late in the evening.
If you cannot sleep after about 20 minutes, get up, do something calm in dim light, then go back to bed when sleepy.
avoid: Avoid tea, coffee and cola after the afternoon.
Avoid heavy meals, alcohol and smoking close to bedtime.
Do not take sleeping pills that are not prescribed for you.
red_flags: Thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life: call 112 now, or the Tele-MANAS helpline 14416.
Loud snoring with choking or stopping breathing during sleep, noticed by others.
Falling asleep while driving or at work.
Sudden confusion or very unusual behaviour at night.
see_doctor_if: Poor sleep lasts more than 3 to 4 weeks, or affects your daily life.
You feel low, worried or hopeless most days.
You think a medicine or health problem, such as pain or passing urine at night, is affecting your sleep.
sources: MoHFW India: Tele-MANAS mental health helpline 14416

items.title: Mild period pain (menstrual cramps)
items.summary: Cramping pain in the lower belly during periods is common and is usually worst in the first 1 to 2 days.
self_care: Put a hot water bag or warm cloth on your lower belly or back. Check it is not too hot.
Do gentle exercise such as walking, stretching or yoga.
Take a warm bath or shower.
Rest, drink enough water, and eat regular light meals.
Gently massage the lower belly.
avoid: Do not use a very hot bag or sleep with it on the skin. It can cause burns.
Do not take painkillers often without a doctor's advice, especially if you have stomach, kidney or asthma problems.
Avoid smoking. It can make period pain worse.
red_flags: Sudden, severe belly pain, especially if your period is late or you could be pregnant: go to hospital now or call 108.
Fainting, dizziness or a fast heartbeat with pain.
Very heavy bleeding that soaks a pad every hour for 2 hours or more.
Pain with high fever or bad-smelling discharge.
see_doctor_if: Pain stops you from going to school or work, or is getting worse over time.
Pain also happens outside your period, or during or after sex.
Periods are very heavy, last more than 7 days, or are very irregular.
